title: The Model Millionaire
author: Oscar Wilde (王尔德)
summary: 英俊善良但囊中羞涩的青年休吉，在画家好友画室偶遇一名衣衫褴褛的老乞丐模特，出于同情将身上仅剩的主权金币慷慨相赠。第二天他才惊愕发现，这位乞丐模特竟是欧洲首富豪斯伯格男爵……王尔德式风趣机智与善意的喜剧。

paragraphs.author: Oscar Wilde (王尔德)
paragraphs.en:
The Model Millionaire
Oscar Wilde (王尔德)
paragraphs.zh: 《模范百万富翁》 · Oscar Wilde (王尔德)

paragraphs.en: Unless one is wealthy there is no use in being a charming fellow. Romance is the privilege of the rich, not the profession of the unemployed. The poor should be practical and prosaic. It is better to have a permanent income than to be fascinating. These are the great truths of modern life which Hughie Erskine never realised.
paragraphs.zh: 除非一个人腰缠万贯，否则单凭风度翩翩魅力四射是毫无用处的。浪漫情调向来是有钱人的特权，而非无业游民的本钱。穷人理应本分务实、泯然众人。拥有一份旱涝保收的稳定收入，远胜过拥有一副颠倒众生的迷人面孔。然而，休吉·厄斯金对这套现代社会的深刻现实真理向来浑然不知。

paragraphs.en: Poor Hughie! Intellectually, we must admit, he was not of much importance. He never said a brilliant or even an ill-natured thing in his life. But then he was wonderfully good-looking, with his crisp brown hair, his clear-cut profile, and his grey eyes. He was as popular with men as he was with women, and he had every accomplishment except that of making money.
paragraphs.zh: 可怜的休吉！平心而论，从学识才智上讲，他实在算不上什么大人物。他这辈子既没说过什么锦心绣口的妙语，也没吐露过半句尖酸刻薄的坏话。然而，他生得格外英俊出众：卷曲茂密的棕发、轮廓分明的侧颜、一双清澈透亮的灰眼睛。他在男士与女士中间都极具好人缘，掌握着除了“赚钱”之外的一切世家教养与才艺。

paragraphs.en: His father had bequeathed him his cavalry sword, and a History of the Peninsular War in fifteen volumes. Hughie hung the first over his looking-glass, put the second on a shelf between Ruff's Guide and the Sporting Magazine, and lived on two hundred a year that an old aunt allowed him. He had tried everything. He had gone on the Stock Exchange for six months, but what was a butterfly to do among bulls and bears?
paragraphs.zh: 他的老父亲去世时给他留下一把佩剑和一套十五卷本的《半岛战争史》。休吉把佩剑挂在穿衣镜上方，将大部头历史书摆在赛马指南与体育杂志中间，靠一位老姑妈每年施舍的两百英镑勉强糊口。他也曾努力尝试过各种营生：去证券交易所混迹了半年，可一只轻盈的蝴蝶能在凶狠的牛市与熊市之间扑腾出什么名堂？

paragraphs.en: He had been a tea-merchant for a little longer, but he had soon got tired of pekoe and souchong. Then he had tried selling dry sherry. That did not do; the sherry was a little too dry. Ultimately he became nothing, a delightful, ineffectual young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
paragraphs.zh: 后来他又转行做过一阵茶叶生意，但很快就对各色红茶绿茶厌烦透顶。接着他又尝试推销雪莉酒，但生意冷清得很，酒实在太干涩难咽。最终，他成了无业游民——一个除了完美无瑕的俊美容颜外别无所长、讨人喜欢却一事无成的英俊绅士。

paragraphs.en: To make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired Colonel who had lost his temper and his digestion in India, and had never found either of them again. Laura adored him, and he was ready to kiss the ground she walked upon.
paragraphs.zh: 更糟糕的是，他偏偏还坠入了爱河。他心仪的姑娘名叫萝拉·默顿，是一位退役上校的掌上明珠。这位老上校当年在印度服役时败坏了脾气和胃口，回国后两者就再也没调理好过。萝拉深爱着休吉，而休吉恨不得亲吻她走过的每一寸泥土。

paragraphs.en: The Colonel was very fond of Hughie, but would not hear of any engagement. 'Come to me, my boy, when you have got ten thousand pounds of your own, and we will see about it,' he used to say; and Hughie looked very glum on those days, and had to go to Laura for consolation.
paragraphs.zh: 上校本人其实挺喜欢休吉，但对两人的订婚却绝口不松口。“小伙子，等你哪天自己凭本事赚足了一万英镑，再来找我谈吧，到时候咱们再商量商量，”老上校常这么说。每逢此时，休吉便愁眉苦脸、唉声叹气，只能跑去萝拉那里寻求温存安慰。

paragraphs.en: One morning, on his way to Holland Park, he dropped in to see a great friend of his, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. Indeed, few people escape that nowadays. But he was also an artist, and artists are rather rare. Personally he was a strange rough fellow, with a freckled face, and a red ragged beard. However, when he took up the brush he was a real master.
paragraphs.zh: 一天清晨，休吉在前往荷兰公园的途中顺路拐去拜访挚友艾伦·特雷弗。特雷弗是一名画家——事实上如今年头画画的人多如牛毛，但他同时是一位真正的艺术大师，而大师向来凤毛麟角。特雷弗相貌粗犷古怪，长着一脸雀斑和乱蓬蓬的红胡子，然而一旦拿起画笔，他便是一位不折不扣的丹青妙手。

paragraphs.en: When Hughie came in he found Trevor putting the finishing touches to a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar-man. The beggar himself was standing on a raised platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wizened old man, with a face like wrinkled parchment, and a most piteous expression.
paragraphs.zh: 当休吉推门走进画室时，特雷弗正巧在一幅逼真的等身乞丐油画前做最后的润色收尾。乞丐模特本人正站在画室角落的高台上：那是一个干瘪佝偻的耄耋老叟，面容宛如一张布满折痕的风干羊皮纸，神情凄楚凄苦，令人动容。

paragraphs.en: Over his shoulders was flung a coarse brown cloak, all tears and tatters; his thick boots were patched and cobbled, and with one hand he leant on a rough stick, while with the other he held out his battered hat for alms.
paragraphs.zh: 老人的肩头披着一件粗糙的褐色破斗篷，千疮百孔、褴褛不堪；厚重的旧皮靴补丁叠着补丁，他一手拄着一根粗糙的拐杖，另一只干枯的手捧着一顶破破烂烂的帽子乞讨施舍。

paragraphs.en: 'What an amazing model!' whispered Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. 'An amazing model?' shouted Trevor at the top of his voice; 'I should think so! Such beggars as he are not to be met with every day. A trouvaille, mon cher; a living Velasquez!'
paragraphs.zh: “多么令人惊叹的模特啊！”休吉与朋友握手时轻声赞叹。“惊叹？”特雷弗扯开破锣般的嗓门叫嚷道，“那还用说！像他这么极品的叫花子打着灯笼都找不着！简直是个无价之宝，我亲爱的朋友，活生生的委拉斯开兹画中人！”

paragraphs.en: 'Poor old chap!' said Hughie, 'how miserable he looks! But I suppose, to you painters, his face is his fortune?' 'Certainly,' replied Trevor, 'you don't want a beggar to look happy, do you?'
paragraphs.zh: “可怜的老人家！”休吉叹息道，“他看起来多么凄惨绝望啊！不过我想对你们画家而言，他的苦难面孔反倒成了财运吧？”“那是自然，”特雷弗理所当然地答道，“你总不能指望一个乞丐满脸堆笑吧？”

paragraphs.en: 'How much does a model get for sitting?' asked Hughie, as he found himself a comfortable seat on a divan. 'A shilling an hour.' 'And how much do you get for your picture, Alan?' 'Oh, for this I get two thousand guineas!'
paragraphs.zh: “当模特坐在这儿能拿多少报酬？”休吉在长沙发上找了个舒服的位置坐下问道。“一小时一个先令。”“那艾伦，你这幅画能卖多少钱？”“噢，这幅画嘛，买家出价两千基尼金币！”

paragraphs.en: 'Well, I think the model ought to have a percentage,' cried Hughie, laughing; 'they work quite as hard as you do.' 'Nonsense, nonsense! Why, look at the trouble of laying on the paint alone, and standing all day long at one's easel!'
paragraphs.zh: “依我看，模特理应分得一定比例的提成，”休吉笑着调侃道，“人家站着摆姿势出的苦力可一点不比你少。”“胡说八道！少扯淡了！你瞧瞧单是调色涂抹颜料有多费劲，整天杵在画架前腿都要断了！”

paragraphs.en: After some time the servant came in, and told Trevor that the frame-maker wanted to speak to him. 'Don't run away, Hughie,' he said, as he went out, 'I will be back in a moment.' The old beggar-man took advantage of Trevor's absence to rest for a moment on a wooden bench.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，仆人进门通报，说裱画框的匠人有要事找特雷弗。“休吉，别急着走，”特雷弗出门时嘱咐道，“我马上回来。”老乞丐趁着画家离开的空档，拖着疲惫的身躯在木凳上稍事歇息。

paragraphs.en: He looked so forlorn and wretched that Hughie could not help pitying him, and felt in his pockets to see what money he had. All he could find was a sovereign and some coppers. 'Poor old fellow,' he thought to himself, 'he wants it more than I do, though it means no hackney carriages for a fortnight.' And he walked across the studio and slipped the sovereign into the beggar's hand.
paragraphs.zh: 老人神情落寞凄凉，休吉不由得顿生恻隐之心。他摸了摸衣兜，想看看自己带了多少零钱。兜里翻来翻去，只有一枚金灿灿的主权金币和几个铜子儿。“可怜的老人家，”休吉心想，“他显然比我更需要这枚金币，大不了我接下来半个月出门都不雇马车步行就是了。”于是他穿过画室，悄悄把那枚主权金币塞进了老乞丐的手心。

paragraphs.en: The old man started, and a faint smile flitted across his withered lips. 'Thank you, sir,' he said, 'thank you.' Then Trevor arrived, and Hughie took his leave, blushing a little at what he had done. He spent the day with Laura, got a charming scolding for his extravagance, and had to walk home.
paragraphs.zh: 老乞丐浑身微微一颤，枯瘪的双唇掠过一丝淡淡的笑意。“谢谢您，先生，”老人呢喃道，“谢谢您。”这时特雷弗回到了画室，休吉为自己的善举略感不好意思，便起身告辞了。那天他陪萝拉待了一整天，因为挥霍金币被心上人娇嗔地数落了一顿，最后只能一路徒步走回了家。

paragraphs.en: That night he strolled into the Palette Club about eleven o'clock, and found Trevor sitting by himself in the smoking-room drinking hock and seltzer. 'Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?' he said, as he lit his cigarette.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚大约十一点，休吉漫步走进调色板俱乐部，发现特雷弗正独自坐在吸烟室里啜饮着白葡萄酒与苏打水。“嗨艾伦，你那幅画顺利收尾完工了吗？”休吉点上一支香烟问道。

paragraphs.en: 'Finished and framed, my boy!' answered Trevor; 'and, by-the-bye, you have made a conquest. That old model you saw is quite devoted to you. I had to tell him all about you—who you were, where you lived, what your income was, what prospects you had—'
paragraphs.zh: “不仅画完了，画框都装好了，我的老弟！”特雷弗眉飞色舞地回答，“顺便告诉你，你今天可是征服了一位忠实粉丝！那个老模特对你念念不忘、赞不绝口。我不得不把你的底细一五一十全告诉了他：你是谁、住哪儿、年收入多少、有什么前途打算……”

paragraphs.en: 'My dear Alan,' cried Hughie, 'I shall probably find him waiting for me when I go home. But of course you are only joking. Poor old wretch! I wish I could do something for him. I think it is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable.'
paragraphs.zh: “我亲爱的艾伦，”休吉哭笑不得地嚷道，“照你这么说，等会儿我回家他保准蹲在门口等我呢！不过你肯定是在拿我寻开心。可怜的老人家！真希望我能再帮他一把，世上竟然有人生活得如此悲惨凄凉，实在太叫人揪心了。”

paragraphs.en: 'Why, man, you gave him a sovereign!' 'Yes, but it's nothing to a man who has two thousand a year like you.' 'Now, listen to me,' said Trevor, smiling; 'that old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all London to-morrow without overdrawing his account. He is Baron Hausberg.'
paragraphs.zh: “老兄，你今天可是塞给了他一整枚主权金币啊！”“是啊，可比起你这种年入两千基尼的大画家，我那点钱算什么。”“你给我洗耳恭听好了，”特雷弗神秘地微笑道，“你口中那个‘穷老头’，实际上是全欧洲屈指可数的大富豪之一！他明天哪怕买下大半个伦敦，银行账户都绝不会透支一分钱！他就是大名鼎鼎的豪斯伯格男爵！”

paragraphs.en: 'Baron Hausberg!' cried Hughie. 'Good heavens! I gave him a sovereign!' and he sank into an armchair the picture of dismay. 'Gave him a sovereign!' shouted Trevor, and he burst into a roar of laughter. 'My dear boy, you'll never see it again. Son affaire c'est l'argent des autres.'
paragraphs.zh: “豪斯伯格男爵？！”休吉惊得眼珠子都快掉出来了，“天哪！我……我竟然施舍了他一枚金币！”他一屁股瘫坐在扶手椅里，神情沮丧到了极点。“施舍了他一枚金币！”特雷弗乐得拍腿狂笑，“我亲爱的老弟，你这辈子是别想见着那枚金币了！”

paragraphs.en: 'I think you might have told me, Alan,' said Hughie sulkily, 'and not have let me make such a fool of myself.' 'Well, to begin with, Hughie, it never entered my mind that you went about distributing alms in that reckless way. I can understand your kissing a pretty model, but giving a sovereign to an ugly one—by Jove, no!'
paragraphs.zh: “艾伦，你早该提醒我的，”休吉懊恼地咕哝着，“省得我像个白痴一样出尽洋相。”“咳，老弟，打死我也想不到你竟然大方到随手乱发金币的地步啊！你要是亲吻一个漂亮的俏女模特我倒能理解，可给一个脏兮兮的丑老头塞金币——老天爷啊，谁能想得到！”

paragraphs.en: The next morning, as he was at breakfast, the servant brought him up a card on which was written: 'Monsieur Gustave Naudin, d'un de la part de M. le Baron Hausberg.' 'I suppose he has come for an apology,' said Hughie to himself; and he told the servant to show the visitor up.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天清晨，休吉正在吃早餐，仆人递上一张精美名片，上面赫然写着：“豪斯伯格男爵阁下特派代表：古斯塔夫·诺丹先生”。“我想人家肯定是登门来讨说法的，”休吉暗自叫苦，吩咐仆人将贵客请上楼来。

paragraphs.en: An elderly gentleman with gold spectacles and grey hair came into the room. 'Have I the honour of addressing Monsieur Erskine?' Hughie bowed. 'I have come from Baron Hausberg. The Baron—' 'I beg, sir, that you will offer him my sincerest apologies,' stammered Hughie.
paragraphs.zh: 一位戴着金丝眼镜、头发花白的年长绅士步入房间。“请问我有幸会晤厄斯金先生本人吗？”休吉局促地欠身致意。“我奉豪斯伯格男爵之命前来。男爵阁下他——”“先生，我恳求您转达我对他老人家最诚挚的万分歉意，”休吉结结巴巴地抢白道。

paragraphs.en: 'The Baron,' said the old gentleman with a smile, 'has commissioned me to bring you this letter'; and he extended a sealed envelope. On the outside was written, 'A wedding present to Hugh Erskine and Laura Merton, from an old beggar,' and inside was a cheque for £10,000.
paragraphs.zh: “男爵阁下，”老绅士温和地微笑着说，“特意委托我将这封信转交给您。”说着递上一只封漆火漆的精美信封。信封的封套上赫然题写着一行优雅的小字：“一位老乞丐赠予休·厄斯金与萝拉·默顿的新婚贺礼”，而在信封里面，静静躺着一张整整一万英镑的现金支票！

paragraphs.en: When they were married Alan Trevor was the best-man, and the Baron made a speech at the wedding-breakfast. 'Millionaire models,' remarked Alan, 'are rare enough; but, by Jove, model millionaires are rarer still!'
paragraphs.zh: 当休吉与萝拉喜结连理的大喜之日，艾伦·特雷弗担任了伴郎，豪斯伯格男爵更是在婚宴早餐上发表了热情洋溢的致辞。艾伦意味深长地感叹道：“当模特的百万富翁固然凤毛麟角，但凭良心讲，像男爵这般堪称‘道德模范’的真正百万富翁，更是人间少有啊！”
